findings.finding: Norwegian political momentum against new data centres sharpened in the two sessions before the print: on 28 Oct Senterpartiet joined SV, MDG, Rødt and KrF in calling for a temporary halt on new data centres until summer and proposed raising their electricity tax from 7 to over 30 øre/kWh; on 29 Oct Rødt announced an urgent motion and an NVE report warned of a power deficit. This bears on MDATA's Norwegian pipeline (Averøya, Surnadal, Sauda and Gloppen awaiting grid allocation, plus the Oslo metro sites). Existing centres and projects under construction are exempt, and Ap, Høyre and FrP oppose a halt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no prior policy surprise on this name; on 28 Oct, the day the Sp turn was reported (09:26 CET), MDATA closed +4.8% (13.36 -> 14.00), so the market did not sell this line
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-30 — only through management's commentary at the 09:30 CET webcast; any Storting vote or budget deal comes later
findings.original_quote: Senterpartiet krever en midlertidig stans for nye datasentre frem til sommeren. ... Sp slutter seg dermed til SV, MDG, Rødt og KrF, som også vil stanse nye datasentre midlertidig. Høyre, Ap og Frp vil ikke stanse utbyggingen mens nye regler utformes. ... Eksisterende datasentre og prosjekter under bygging skal få fortsette. ... øke elavgiften for datasentre fra 7 øre til over 30 øre per kilowattime. [Sp demands a temporary halt on new data centres until the summer ... joining SV, MDG, Rødt and KrF; Høyre, Ap and FrP will not halt the build-out ... existing data centres and projects under construction may continue ... raise the electricity tax for data centres from 7 øre to over 30 øre per kWh.]
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The story is domestic-press only (E24/NTB/Aftenposten), and the NVE report and Rødt motion land on 29 Oct, the window's opening day. If it were fully priced, the 28 Oct session would have fallen rather than risen +4.8% and the five-day run-up would not be +15.8%. Against that: Ap, Høyre and FrP hold a clear majority against a halt, the company has not said it is exposed, and a large share of the portfolio is in Finland, Estonia, Sweden and Italy. So this is macro-to-company transmission, sized small.
findings.independence: https://e24.no/i/PgV5rb/datasentre-tror-det-er-klokt-at-stortinget-venter (29 Oct: the energy minister asks the Storting to wait for the government's own measures, 'in the near future'; Rødt files an urgent halt motion; NVE warns of a power deficit). It is the same story thread, so not independent on direction.

findings.finding: Board members bought MDATA shares in seven separate notified transactions from 22 Jul to 21 Sep 2026 at NOK 11.95-15.37, the latest 32,920 shares by Lars Schedin at NOK 15.37, above today's NOK 14.14.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none measurable; the buying ran through the September rally to 17.88 and was followed by the October drawdown to 12.28
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: every buy was notified publicly within a day. What is left is that insiders bought above the current price ahead of a report they had sight of. If the market had fully priced that, it would not have retraced 30% from the 5 Oct high.

findings.finding: The H1 report guided 'potential sales in the second half of 2026' and cited LOIs on two sales-ready projects (marketing of Hämeenlinna and SE4). No sale had been announced on NewsWeb by 29 Oct, so the Q3 report is the first scheduled update on whether that guide holds, firms or slips.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: one prior print: H1 on 26 Aug moved +3.2% on the day and -4.4% the next; the announcements of a grid connection and the 100% Hämeenlinna buy-out on 24-25 Aug moved +10.1% and +4.7%
findings.why_not_priced: Its direction is unknown, so it is sized at 0 with a wide band. It is the line where a large move would come from, and nothing sourced says which way it goes. A sale would more likely come as a separate inside-information release than inside the report.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly negative (Norwegian policy) against a mildly positive priced lean (+0.78, which is the run-up term alone) and a +15.8% five-day rebound; the stock already absorbed the Sp news on the way up, which is why p_up sits only two points under 50.
language_note: Norwegian domestic press (E24/NTB) carried the 28-29 Oct political turn on data centres: Sp joining the parties that want a halt, Sp's electricity-tax proposal of 7 -> 30+ øre/kWh, Rødt's urgent motion and the energy minister asking the Storting to wait. None of it appeared in any English source found on this name, and it is the only fresh item in the hunt
the issuer's own filings are English-only on NewsWeb (only Euronext's 2026 admission notice had a Norwegian twin), so the filing half added nothing local
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'too small about the move': the release carries a qualitative outlook whose revision is the line in play and nothing is pre-released, so abs_move_pct went from 5.5 to 6.5 (European new-numbers base about 7%, trimmed because the P&L is immaterial)

'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company has said it': the Norwegian policy finding went from -0.8 to -0.6, because MDATA has not stated its exposure and the stock rose on the news day
insider-buying finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2: public within a day, so mostly priced
the bar is unsourced, so every finding stays capped small and print_vs_bar_pct stays 0
